newsitem.title: UK: Dollar marches on the mark, bourses buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Dollar marches on the mark, bourses buoyant.

text.p: The dollar romped ahead against the mark on Tuesday and European bourses also prospered, with British blue chips breaking records before falling back after a weaker start on Wall Street.
The dollar, which sneaked above the psychological 1.50 marks barrier in early European trade, continued to firm as the day progressed, nudging the 1.5060 level.
Its rise followed comments on Monday by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that central bank governors in Basle had agreed a strong dollar was "in the interests of all".

Leading shares in London, Frankfurt and Paris all got a leg-up after Monday's peformance by the Dow Jones industrial average, which posted its biggest one-day gain in over a month to close 1.3 percent up.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 index jumped more than 20 points to a record 3,933.6, surpassing its previous record of 3,922.1 set on August 28. However, after a weaker start on Wall Street Tuesday, it fell back to around the 3,920 level.
The Dow was down about 15 points or a quarter of a percent in early New York trading on what dealers described as predictable profit taking

Analysts said London's gains were also held in check by a lacklustre performance by government bonds, overshadowed by worries that Britain will cut interest rates further to stoke pre-election growth regardless of the inflation risk.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended a lively floor trade session higher, cheered by Wall Street's performance on Monday and the ever-strengthening dollar. The 30-share DAX index ended at 2,570.95 points, up 22.22.

The same motors, plus gains in the French franc, propelled Paris shares, which started firmer and quickly strengthened. However, like the FTSE, the main CAC-40 index fell back from its highs in the afternoon under the influence of New York's shaky start.
Stock and currency markets remained gripped by interest rate prospects following last Friday's U.S. jobs data showing lower unemployment and stronger earnings.

U.S. producer and consumer price data -- due Thursday and Friday -- will be scrutinised for fresh signs of inflation pressures. Many traders and investors are betting on a rise of 0.25 percentage point in U.S. interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
Opinions are mixed as to whether the central bank will decide this time to raise or leave interest rates unchanged, perhaps until after the November 5 presidential election.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5065 marks and 109.70 yen compared with late European levels on Monday of 1.4935 and 109.15.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
By 1000 GMT the Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 6.4 points at 3,917.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 18.37 at 2,038.67.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 22.22 at 2,570.95.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold Fixed at $383.10 compared with Monday's close of $383.45. Silver was steady at $5.10.
